resources.string: The Xperia Z1–style venetian-blinds unlock, on modern Android.
Swipe up or down to unlock
When the screen turns off, the blinds lock screen is placed on top of the system one. Swipe it to unlock — your PIN, pattern or fingerprint still apply.
Needed on Android 10+ so the lock screen can appear when the screen turns off.
Stops the system from killing the app in the background.

Android 15+: if “Display over other apps” is greyed out, open App info → ⋮ menu → “Allow restricted settings”, then grant it. Xiaomi / Oppo / Vivo: also allow “Show on lock screen” and “Open new windows while running in background” under Other permissions.
Allow “Display over other apps” for Blinds Lock
Android only lets apps read your wallpaper with “Files and media” access. Blinds Lock uses it just to copy your wallpaper.

On Android 13 and newer, Android only lets apps read your wallpaper with “All files access”.

Blinds Lock uses it only to copy your lock-screen wallpaper, and keeps it in sync when you change wallpaper. The app has no internet access.

If you’d rather not grant it, use “Choose image” and pick the same photo instead.
Couldn’t read the current wallpaper. Try “Choose image” instead.
“Use current wallpaper” copies your lock-screen wallpaper (or home wallpaper if there isn’t a separate one). Live and video wallpapers can’t be copied.

Like the Xperia lock screen: swipe left or right on the clock to flip between widgets. The last page is “+” to add more. Any widget your apps offer works: music controls, weather, calendar, clocks, notes, and more. Widgets turn with the blinds when you unlock.
No widgets yet. Only the clock is shown.
None of your apps offer widgets.
Widget added to the lock screen
Blinds that move with your finger
Your phone uses a PIN, pattern or password.
No PIN/pattern: swiping the blinds unlocks straight to your home screen.

No app can skip your PIN. That is what keeps your phone safe. You can still get “swipe and you’re in” almost every time:

• Fingerprint while the screen is off (Samsung: Fingerprints → “Fingerprint always on”). Touch the sensor to wake the phone. It is already unlocked, so the blinds open straight to your home screen.
• Face recognition: after you swipe, the system checks your face and continues without asking for the PIN.
• Smart Lock / Extend Unlock (trusted places, your watch or earbuds): while trusted, swiping the blinds unlocks directly. Blinds Lock detects this automatically.
• Lock automatically after… (Samsung: Lock screen → Secure lock settings): no PIN if the screen was only off for a short time.

The PIN is then only asked occasionally, as Android requires.

Ticks as each slat passes under your finger (stronger the faster you swipe), a rising click when you have swiped far enough, and a rattle as the blinds open. Follows your system “Touch feedback” setting. Lock/unlock sounds play only when your ringer is on (not silent/vibrate). If you hear double clicks, turn off Android’s own “Screen lock sound” in Sound settings.

• Swipe up or down. The slats under your finger turn and twist toward where you touch. Fast swipes make them flap more.
• Best experience: set your system screen lock to Swipe or None, or use fingerprint / face unlock — the blinds then open straight onto your home screen.
• With a PIN or pattern, swipe the blinds and the system asks for it; the blinds open after it is entered.
• Android does not let normal apps replace the system lock screen itself, so this app shows its own screen above it. The phone stays exactly as secure as before.
• The app has no internet permission and no accessibility service.
